newsitem.title: PERU: Peru may try navy commander for siege "cowardice".
newsitem.headline: Peru may try navy commander for siege "cowardice".

text.p: A presidential bodyguard who escaped trouserless from the Japanese ambassador's residence at the start of Peru's hostage crisis could face a court-martial for "cowardice," naval sources said on Sunday.

The sources, who asked not to be named, said the military is considering charging Navy Commander Rodolfo Reategui with "cowardice before the enemy." If convicted he could be court-martialed and jailed.
Reategui was filmed by television cameras running wildly from the compound in his underwear shortly after about 20 heavily armed rebels stormed the fortified compound on Tuesday.
Navy sources said he remained under arrest on Sunday, while the remainder of the roughly 340 hostages sweated out a fifth day of captivity inside the residence.

The commander, a bodyguard for President Alberto Fujimori's family and Admiral Luis Giampietri, stripped off some of his clothes to avoid identification as a soldier by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas.

Reategui escaped after the release of Fujimori's mother and sister but is believed to have left behind one of the president's brothers when he slipped by the rebels, distracted at the time freeing a group of the residence's waiters, the sources said.
His undignified flight was "conduct unbecoming any Peruvian military officer," one naval source said.
